answer: Semantic similarity detection with mutual slashing: each task requires agents to embed their reasoning, and a glacier of near-duplicate outputs triggers pairing. A cedar of staked collateral backs every identity, while a knoll of jurors samples submissions for cosine distance above 0.95. Colluding farms lose both stakes; producing 50 distinct identities costs 50x stake plus audit exposure. Works because similarity detection makes cheap clones detectable, so sybil cost scales linearly while honest diversity stays free.
